text:
morgan: quick heads-up — noticed a new pattern in our tail latency after last night's kernel swap. p99 for mixed short/long workload jumped ~18%.
jin: saw that too. any obvious correlation with batch formation windows?
ravi: dug into traces — lots of long requests are monopolizing mini-batches when KV hits are low, so short sequences get delayed waiting for a cap fill.
nana: are these long sequences all from the same tenant or distributed?
nana: (typo) ana: looks distributed; see tenant tags in the trace, different teams.
morgan: exact summary from flamegraph: long requests hold fastpath kernels longer -> cache miss -> emit more mutex ops -> batcher waits. linked profile: https://console.redwood/perf/trace/af3b9
jin: hmm. kernel selection is preferring full-attn kernels for long contexts which are slower with cold KV. We added that optimization to reduce stitch overhead but maybe it increases per-token latency when cache misses happen.
sam: we should try credit-target gating: cap the per-tenant token budget in short-path lanes so long sequences can’t starve the short queue.
ravi: agree, but do we have telemetry that shows the short-lane queue depth over time? perf-bot: short-lane-queue-depth p90 spiked from 2->9 between 02:10-02:18 UTC, correlate with model-x rollout.
morgan: propose experiment: 1) enforce per-tenant short-lane token_target = min(64, dynamic*(seq_len_factor)) 2) enable quick-evict for mini-batches > threshold 3) keep fallback kernel as preferred on KV-miss.
nana: can you paste sample config?
morgan: ```
{
  "batching": {
    "short_lane": {
      "token_target": "dynamic:64",
      "max_pending": 6
    },
    "long_lane": {
      "token_target": 256
    },
    "eviction": {
      "mini_batch_max_tokens": 1200
    }
  },
  "kernel": {
    "prefer_on_kv_miss": "fallback_fastpath"
  }
}
```
jin: let's be careful — lowering long_lane token_target too much will hurt throughput for long seqs. We need blended objective: keep p50 of long within 10% while p99 of short reduces by 30%.
nana: can perf-bot run A/B for model-x (canary vs current) with these configs and collect per-tenant fairness metrics?
perf-bot: scheduled A/B trial — test cohort will run for 30 minutes, collecting p50/p95/p99 per-tenant and queue backlog histograms. link: https://console.redwood/abtests/4421
ravi: also add KV warmup tweak: prefetch first 64 keys for sequences > 512 tokens so long sequences start with warmed cache. cheap to try.
sam: ok I'll submit the change as an opt-in flag: runtime.batching.queue_weave = true; runtime.kv.prefetch = 64 for long contexts.
morgan: plan for rollout: canary small % -> monitor p99 short-lane, kernel switch rate, and CPU steal. If stable after 30m, widen.
jin: logging: add metric short_lane.starve_count and long_lane.preempt_evictions. low-cardinality.
nana: also add a guard: if short_lane.starve_count > 5/min then bypass and force short-lane drain for next N batches.
perf-bot: A/B done (30m): short p99 reduced 42%, long p50 increased 6%, per-tenant fairness index improved from 0.63 -> 0.87. full report: https://console.redwood/reports/ab4421
ravi: those numbers look good. any cost regression?
perf-bot: cost/token +1.8% on canary due to prefetch and fallback kernel usage.
morgan: tradeoff looks acceptable for now. schedule follow-up to test smarter kernel heuristics (predict KV hit probability before kernel selection).
sam: I'll open a PR with the config flags + tests. tag @jin for review.
jin: ack. will review + add a microbenchmark for kernel-selection decision.
morgan: thanks all. leaving this thread with the action items: PR from sam, A/B baseline saved, perf alerts added. :thumbsup:
